quest.title: Waking from the Great Dream
quest.description: In the Primordial Sea, face Narzissenkreuz's dream of salvation.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x35000

chapter.num: In the Wake of Narcissus: Act III
chapter.title: Waking From the Great Dream

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: I... I sense "reason." Visitors, are you the successors to Narzissenkreuz, or are you a threat?

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: You have drawn your weapons. I see your answer.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Narzissenkreuz...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? This thing's Narzissenkreuz?

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: If you have heard my name, then you know of my quest to save the world, and there is a chance that you can be saved.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: You draw your weapons at me only because you have been misled by untruths. But this is no time for me to waste my powers.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Wonder and rejoice. When all is over, I shall explain, I shall demonstrate. But now, place the Holy Blade in my hand and flee to safety.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're not giving you the Holy Blade.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Foolish, foolish. But I forgive you and will save you nevertheless.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: I can sense that the four orthants have been reversed. But the tree of flowing is not yet complete.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: It is no longer possible to save everyone. I will extend my benevolence as far as possible, even if it makes an overdraft of my own life force.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: If only five in ten can be saved, I will strive to save six in ten.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Now, I shall come to take the Holy Blade.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Impossible... I had already reached the stage of "no return." How have I fallen to this point?

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: And I have lost all control of the Primordial Sea.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Why, why has this happened? Why, why did you do this?

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: The new world cannot be born. All will die in a shell, a husk of a dream!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon reckons you're the one who should try waking up from your dream.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The end of the world is the kind of thing that everyone should work together to stop.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: I see. The Holy Blade is not on my side. With each swing, it cuts through the universal will that surrounds me.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Until, at last, my weak, ordinary self has returned to its physical body.

choices.text: The Primordial Sea won't overflow its banks so soon.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: Indeed, I can sense changes in the values originally entered into the world-formula.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: Someone has seized control of the life-force, and someone has opened the beast-realm.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: And then, there is one more variable. That is you.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: The person fated to see the all-consuming whale put to flight. The one who shall witness all.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: I see, I see.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: I once dreamed of becoming one just like you. But that dream is now shattered.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: All I have done is meaningless. An empty dream.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: No, less than a dream, even. A dream is at least harmless. But I... No, you, and they... have paid so much for all I have done.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Narzissenkreuz.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: Oh, it's you. I didn't see you there.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Do you know who I actually am?

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: Names are just labels. But yes, I am most familiar with the two colors that mix in your soul.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: Director Lyris does not know what has happened. She just holds onto Mary-Ann, who herself still clings to life.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: She cannot understand such a complex present and future, and hopes just to retain the past. And so, she does the only thing she can.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: My name is Ann.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: In that case, hello, Ann.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: I am willing to forgive you.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: What an odd thing to say. From the very start, my plans have had lofty and sacred aims. Selfishness has never come into it.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: None may judge or criticize me, nor do I need forgiveness.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Your aims may have been lofty, but your insanity has harmed many.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: You did not even enter the formula correctly... and what's wrong with being forgiven for a mistake?

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: ...You are right. I apologize.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: So please, Narzissenkreuz, come back with us. There are other people you need to see.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This guy seems to have become much more cooperative. But a request like that...

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: Of course.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Doesn't this sorta thing usually require some inner struggle and hours of persuasion?

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: As I have said before, I do not feel that I have done anything wrong. My mission has failed, but the world has been saved nonetheless.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: Let others mock and curse me. I am empty within now. Only one desire remains.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What is it?

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: I, too, wish to return to the very beginning — to the time before the Narzissenkreuz heroes set off on their journey.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: But that's impossible. We are not masters of our own fate. I no longer even have the power to determine my own dreams.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: #Well, Knight {NICKNAME}, when you're ready, we'll proceed to reseal the primordial waters, and then we'll leave this place.

choices.text: That creature has already been defeated.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: I should have sensed the changes in the values originally entered into the world-formula. A "variable" has descended upon this world.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: Not everything from outside the universe can be called a "presence" or "variable."

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: But it seems I overlooked one nonetheless. You.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: The witness of all, the recorder of all, the designer of all.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: Only one who is worth a world can bear that title.
